title: The Runesmith of Turing
subtitle: Forging runic blades inscribed with Boolean logic that only cut falsehood.
quote: A blade tempered in pure truth needs no edge; it simply separates true from false.
excerpt: In the subterranean volcanic forges of Val-Dor, a dwarven master hammers swords that do not cut flesh, but sever false propositions and illusionary phantoms with Boolean certainty.
body:
Dwarf Master Brokk did not forge swords to slay dragons or pierce dragon scale.

"Any fool with an iron bar and coal can make an edge sharp enough to draw blood," Brokk growled, plunging a glowing white steel bar into a trough of enchanted quench oil. "I forge weapons that cut through lies."

On the anvil rested Veritas, a longsword forged from celestial meteoric iron. Along its fuller ran five carved runic glyphs that glowed with cold, brilliant blue light: AND, OR, NOT, XOR, and EQUALS.

The Trial of the Shadow Lord

When the Shadow King marched upon the citadel with an army of ten thousand mirror illusions, no ordinary arrows could stop them. For every phantom struck down by an archer, two more appeared in its place.

The King of the Dwarves drew Veritas.

He swung the blade through the air. The edge did not touch flesh. Instead, the NOT rune flared with blinding daylight, evaluating the ontological predicate of the army: isReal(Entity) == false.

"Where falsehood stands, truth needs only be stated once.
The boolean evaluator never compromises."

With a crack like shattered glass, all ten thousand illusions vanished simultaneously into thin air, leaving only a solitary, trembling sorcerer standing alone on the cobblestones. The compiler of justice had evaluated to clean zero.
